original.target_description: Single cross-sectional structural equation model: direct association of latent financial communication with financial conflict among U.S. emerging adults currently in romantic relationships; relationship quality corresponds to the supplied relationship satisfaction description.

n.sample_role: individual participants in the analytical SEM sample
n.exclusions: From 4,182 recruited U.S. emerging adults, included only those reporting a current romantic relationship. Missing control data (<1.7% each) handled using full information maximum likelihood; no missing main-variable data.
n.location: Printed p. 6 (PDF p. 8), Data and Sample; printed p. 12 (PDF p. 14), Table 2 note; missingness printed p. 9 (PDF p. 11)
n.quote: Our analytical sample (N = 1,950) included those from a variety of backgrounds.

es.location: Printed p. 11 (PDF p. 13), Structural Equation Model; printed p. 12 (PDF p. 14), Table 2, Financial Communication row / financial conflict column
es.quote:
Couples’ financial communication was directly associated with their relationship quality (β = .57; p < .001) and financial conflict (β
= -.27; p < .001).

replication.target_description: Relationship between financial communication and financial disagreements. Published2024 article pp.2536–2538, cross-sectional actor and partner effects, plus longitudinal effects pp.2538–2539. Locator does not distinguish spouse, actor/partner path or model.

n.sample_role: Newlywed mixed-gender dyads; final overall analytical sample is1,079, but no unique target test assigned.
n.exclusions: Overall study retains continuous marriages W1–W5 and excludes34 same-gender couples; specific target test remains ambiguous.

es.location: p.2537 Direct effects and Figure1; pp.2538–2539 longitudinal results

notes:
Original title and DOI verified against supplied reference. Supplied original p. 13 discusses these outcomes; coefficients are printed on pp. 11–12. IDs 52/53 share identical original and replication locators and descriptions, as do IDs 54/55; no assignment of different replication sex-specific, actor/partner, cross-sectional or longitudinal paths was inferred from ID order. Original direct association extracted identically within each duplicate pair. Replication DOI landing page returned 403/challenge; OpenAlex and Unpaywall provided no open-access location. One alternate full-text host returned 403. Wiley web view contained only abstract and references, not accepted as full text; no abstract sample size treated as analytic n. Acquisition stopped within the per-paper route budget; no failed route retried.
Source follow-up: Duplicate neutral descriptions52/53 and54/55 provide no mapping to husbands versus wives or actor versus partner paths. No row-order inference made. Satisfaction has four distinct cross-sectional paths (own and partner for each spouse), and financial disagreements likewise has four paths. Rendered PDF p.2537 visually checked. Canonical TXT omits negative signs from financial-disagreement beta coefficients that are visible in PDF narrative and Figure1; parent transcription check required before any signed coefficient extraction. Generic discussion verdict is about mediation hypotheses, not a uniquely identified target path, so reported_success remains null.
